question: Which EV charging programs are open now?
html:
Open EV charging programs

None of the EV charging deadlines we track is still open as of Nov 12, 2026. All three dated EV items in our radar have passed. One lead, the Applegreen Maine NEVI partnership, has no deadline and can still be pursued (CET opportunity radar).

What the radar does not tell us

  • Contract values. The radar has no dollar estimates for any of the four EV items. The owners' award notices or bid tabulations would give those figures.
  • Whether we bid. The radar lists actions but does not record submissions. Our own bid log would confirm which items we answered.
  • New postings since Sep 24, 2026. The radar was generated seven weeks ago. COMMBUYS, RI Purchasing and NH DAS blocked automated access, so coverage in those systems is incomplete (CET opportunity radar).

Where EV fits the growth plan

  • The radar frames the MassDOT and Applegreen work as a multi-state DCFC install pipeline (CET opportunity radar).
  • The growth plan places EV depot charging in Phase 3. It sits alongside SCADA monitoring, solar and storage O&M, and NuWave efficiency. Together these lines are meant to turn one-off bids into recurring contracts (CET growth plan).

EV charging is one of the few lines that can move CET from bid-by-bid project revenue toward the recurring service mix that buyers price higher, so a missed solicitation window costs more than a single job.

Next actions

  1. Refresh the radar. Rerun it for EV and DCFC solicitations posted after Sep 24, 2026. Pull COMMBUYS, RI Purchasing and NH DAS by hand.
  2. Contact Applegreen directly. Offer the installer partnership for its 2026 Maine NEVI sites. Also ask whether the MassDOT installer call produced a shortlist we can still join.
  3. Request the closed results. Ask SRTA and Cambridge for bid tabulations or award notices. Record pricing and winners for future EV bids.
  4. Set up an EV pipeline tracker. Log owner, value, deadline and submission status for each item. That record would answer this question directly next time.

# Open EV charging programs

**None of the EV charging deadlines we track is still open as of Nov 12, 2026.** All three dated EV items in our radar have passed. One lead, the Applegreen Maine NEVI partnership, has no deadline and can still be pursued (CET opportunity radar).

## EV items in the radar

| Program | Owner | Deadline | Status today |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEVI developers' installer call | MassDOT NEVI developers (Global Montello / Applegreen memo) | Oct 31, 2026 | Closed |
| New Bedford DCFC install | SRTA | Oct 9, 2026 | Closed |
| Cambridge neighborhood EV charging (federal-aid) | City of Cambridge | Nov 10, 2026 | Closed two days ago |
| Maine NEVI installer partnership | Applegreen (2026 Maine NEVI awards) | None listed | Still pursuable |

## What the radar does not tell us

- **Contract values.** The radar has no dollar estimates for any of the four EV items. The owners' award notices or bid tabulations would give those figures.
- **Whether we bid.** The radar lists actions but does not record submissions. Our own bid log would confirm which items we answered.
- **New postings since Sep 24, 2026.** The radar was generated seven weeks ago. COMMBUYS, RI Purchasing and NH DAS blocked automated access, so coverage in those systems is incomplete (CET opportunity radar).

## Where EV fits the growth plan

- The radar frames the MassDOT and Applegreen work as a multi-state DCFC install pipeline (CET opportunity radar).
- The growth plan places EV depot charging in Phase 3. It sits alongside SCADA monitoring, solar and storage O&M, and NuWave efficiency. Together these lines are meant to turn one-off bids into recurring contracts (CET growth plan).
- The month-36 roadmap assumes about a 25% recurring service mix. That figure is a labelled assumption, not guidance (CET growth plan).

EV charging is one of the few lines that can move CET from bid-by-bid project revenue toward the recurring service mix that buyers price higher, so a missed solicitation window costs more than a single job.

## Next actions

1. **Refresh the radar.** Rerun it for EV and DCFC solicitations posted after Sep 24, 2026. Pull COMMBUYS, RI Purchasing and NH DAS by hand.
2. **Contact Applegreen directly.** Offer the installer partnership for its 2026 Maine NEVI sites. Also ask whether the MassDOT installer call produced a shortlist we can still join.
3. **Request the closed results.** Ask SRTA and Cambridge for bid tabulations or award notices. Record pricing and winners for future EV bids.
4. **Set up an EV pipeline tracker.** Log owner, value, deadline and submission status for each item. That record would answer this question directly next time.
